claims.evidence: Witness report does not include any readable make/model/label; brand/model not readable in the photos.

risks.risk: Unknown exact machine type (single-needle vs overlock/coverstitch/multi-needle) and capability; wrong type can drastically change value.
risks.proof: A clear close-up of the machine’s front/side nameplate or model plate showing make/model and type.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a generic industrial sewing machine setup with unknown function and no confirmed performance.

risks.risk: Working condition not proven (timing, stitch quality, motor health, feed mechanism).
risks.proof: Video of it running and stitching a sample fabric with visible stitch formation and consistent feed (start-to-finish).
risks.if_unproven: Price as not fully tested/unknown working condition.

risks.risk: Missing or incomplete accessories/attachments (presser feet, needles, bobbins, thread guides, manuals) beyond what’s visible.
risks.proof: Inventory photo/clip laid out showing every included accessory with counts (needles, bobbins, feet, manuals, tools).
risks.if_unproven: Price assuming minimal included accessories and no manuals.

risks.risk: Electrical/power compatibility and safety (voltage, plug type, motor/power supply condition).
risks.proof: Photo of the power rating label (voltage/Hz/wattage) plus a short clip showing it powering on and running.
risks.if_unproven: Price with risk of needing electrical/motor servicing or adapter/parts.

risks.risk: Wear/damage not clearly shown (belt condition, oil leaks, rust, needle bar wear, frayed cables).
risks.proof: Close-up clips of belt/motor area, underside, cable condition, and any visible wear points.
risks.if_unproven: Price at worst-case used condition with potential servicing needs.

risks.risk: Cables and setup appear used/not fully packed; possible missing parts or loose components.
risks.proof: Clip showing the full setup assembled and stable (no missing mounts/parts) and all cables connected correctly.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a used setup that may require reassembly/parts replacement.

proof_requests: Send a clear close-up photo of the machine’s make/model/type nameplate (front/side) showing “EMel” and “EM 8500” if true.
Provide a video of the machine running and stitching on fabric (show stitch quality and consistent feed).
Show an itemized inventory of included accessories/attachments with counts (presser feet, needles, bobbins, thread guides, manuals/tools).
Photo of the power rating label (voltage/Hz/wattage) and a clip of powering on safely.
Close-up clips of belt/motor area and any visible wear (cables, needle area, underside).
response.reason: The witness can confirm it’s an industrial sewing machine on a table with thread stands and accessories, but the make/model and—most importantly—working condition and exact type are not verifiable from the report. Without those, a reliable worst-case price can’t be set confidently.
